title: First word: shalom

lines: FOUR LETTERS, MET ONE BY ONE.
cards: Four letters. For weeks they've arrived one at a time. Shin, the letter on the door.
Lamed, the tall one that rises above the line. Vav, the hook, a single upright stroke. And mem, water, in the closed square it takes at the end of a word, one of the five endings.
Today they sit down together, right to left, with two small marks to give them a voice. They make a word said at doors, written in letters, and found at the end of the priestly blessing.
Your first Hebrew word, read on your own.

teach.h: SHIN, AND THE DOT ON THE RIGHT.
teach.b: Shalom. Read it four ways. First, from the right.
Hebrew runs right to left. Shin, with its three arms; the dot on its right arm says sh. On the left arm, it would say s.
Under it, a small T-shaped mark that, in the pronunciation used in Israel, says ah. Sha. Second, the middle.

teach.h: LAMED, THEN VAV WITH A DOT ON TOP.
teach.b: Then vav, with a single dot right on top, which turns it into a vowel: oh. Lo. Third, the end.
The closed square of final mem, which just says m. Sha, lo, m. Shalom.
Fourth, where it lives. At the end of the priestly blessing in Numbers, the last words are "and give thee peace," and in Hebrew the last word is shalom. In the Psalms: "seek peace, and pursue it."
In daily life it's a hello and a goodbye, and it begins the greeting shalom aleichem, peace be upon you.

teach.h: SHALOM AT THE DOOR, IN AND OUT.
teach.b: One word, used at the door coming in and the door going out.
In a few days we'll open the root underneath it. For now the job is simpler: the letters, the dots, and your own voice putting them together.

how: Jewish children learning to read Hebrew sound out words letter by letter with the vowel points; shalom is used as a greeting for hello and goodbye, and in the longer greeting shalom aleichem.

o: shema, the word that opens the morning prayer
bereshit, the opening word of the whole Torah
shalom, the first Hebrew word you read on your own

games.q: shalom, letter by letter — tap the pairs.
p: shin with the dot on the right
vav with a dot on top

s: the dot over shin can sit on either arm, and it changes the sound
on the right it says sh; on the left it says s.
Hebrew is read from left to right
it runs right to left, so shalom starts with shin at the right edge.
it's a hello and a goodbye, and the start of shalom aleichem.

games.q: you're reading shalom for the first time. where do you start?
o: at the left, with the mem.
at the right, with the shin.
in the middle, with the vav.
games.why: at the right. Hebrew runs right to left: shin, lamed, vav, final mem.

practice: Look at the word on the screen and start at the right: the shin and its dot, the tall lamed, the vav with its dot, the closed mem at the end.

Read it slowly, the way a child does the first time, sha, lo, m, then once more, whole: shalom. If there's someone you'd say it to, bring them to mind as you say it; if you pray, you can hold the word for a moment as you sit.

wordCard.voice: First word. Shalom: shin, lamed, vav, final mem, the first Hebrew word you've read yourself, letter by letter. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: peace, a hello and a goodbye; the last word of the priestly blessing.

carryVoice: Your line: shalom, read. Four letters, two marks, and one word that is now yours. Until next time.
